invariantRules.text: Every SoftwareSystem has at least one contained release, an accountable owner, a system criticality and a status in its declared lifecycle.

Every BusinessApplication has an immutable applicationKey minted by the operating organization software-catalogue authority, unique within that operating organization, plus name, purpose, owner, criticality and lifecycle status.
Every ApplicationUsage has applicationRef, organizationalContextRef, purpose, deliveryMode, validFrom and status; entitlement and deployment/runtime references are optional evidence only.
ApplicationUsage remains valid with zero entitlement refs and zero deployment/runtime refs and is never derived from licence or installation.

deliveryMode is one of installed, vendor-hosted, hybrid or unknown; installed requires a resolvable deployment/runtime pair, vendor-hosted forbids an operator-local pair, and unknown records an explicit absent reason.
Installation is a derived view only: the pair of a current WM-SFT-009 deployment occurrence and its operator-controlled WM-SFT-010 runtime environment; it has no minted identifier.
A deployment occurrence is current only when its effective interval covers the query instant and no later successful superseding occurrence for the same target is effective.

Product-to-application and application-to-derived-installation mappings are many-to-many; one installation may support multiple applications and one application may have zero, one or many installations.
A regional deployment alone creates no product, system or application identity; a distinct system or application requires its own owner, enumerated boundary, purpose and criticality.
ModulePlacement records an operator placement independently of vendor module packaging; promotion requires a dated ApplicationPromotion with originPlacementRef and resultingApplicationKey.
ApplicationPromotion creates no product or deployment identity, preserves the originating placement and cannot reuse a parent application key.

A multi-product assembly earns SoftwareSystem identity only with one accountable owner, an enumerated contained release set, system criticality and coordinated change authority; integration alone is a dependency.
A product providing a runtime class remains WM-SFT-001; an operator-controlled execution context is WM-SFT-010, and vendor-hosted execution is not operator runtime by default.

Provenance on system, application, placement, promotion and usage states the creating authority and source evidence; product name, licence, deployment or region alone is forbidden provenance for minting system/application identity.
Legal lifecycle transitions are proposed→approved→active→restricted→active, active/restricted→retired, and any non-retired state→superseded; no other transition is valid.
Retired or superseded system, application, placement, promotion and usage identifiers remain resolvable through tombstone or successor references and are never recycled.
An active BusinessApplication may reference a retired SoftwareSystem only with an effective successor system reference or explicit detached-system justification.
WM-SFT-002 never masters vendor product, licence, deployment occurrence or runtime environment; each referenced layer retains exactly one named writer.

Name, status and timestamps may share a structural vocabulary, but SKU and edition remain product-only; purpose and usage remain WM-SFT-002-only; occurrence time remains deployment-only; platform and node remain runtime-only.
This candidate description does not become authoritative for the reserved slot until the registry row is amended and the shared N4 specification is partitioned.
